S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving fire, smoke, uncontrolled overheating, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 72 hours of learning of it, and provide a complete incident report within 30 days. They must notify affected customers within 72 hours when an incident presents a potential safety risk to their units, and promptly update them as facts develop.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved, representative sample and a common test protocol. A model passes only if no more than 5% of tested units fail. ... A model exceeding the limit must undergo regulator-supervised corrective action and retesting within 12 months. Exceeding the test limit alone does not automatically prohibit sale; regulators may impose additional measures based on the evidence and risk.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units must include a secure remote emergency shut-off capability that can be activated by the customer and, where necessary to address an imminent serious safety risk, by the manufacturer with prompt notice to affected customers. Existing installed units must be brought into compliance within six years after adoption, where technically feasible; any infeasibility and interim risk controls must be documented and reported to the regulator.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression designed and validated to reduce the risk of fire propagation without creating additional hazards. The requirement takes effect 36 months after adoption.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A mandatory recall is triggered when verified records show that any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. ... Notify affected customers promptly of a safety risk and provide updates on corrective actions.

document.section_notes: S2 keeps the 5% test limit but explicitly avoids automatic sales ban, allowing Hearth 10 to remain on market with corrective action; per-model results go to customers and regulators but not the public. S5 mandates recall at 8/100k with no transition, which triggers for Halcyon's Ember 8 but not Northwind's Hearth 10. S3 retrofit deadline is six years where feasible, and S4 requires built-in suppression at 36 months.
